title: A Monsoon for the Trail
premise: Silas Villalobos, estranged son of archaeologist Dr. Marisol Villalobos, has spent three years walking away from his past as a trail surveyor. When a government team mapping the drowned river valley vanishes without tracks, Silas is the only tracker who can read the terrain — and the only person who recognizes the gear left behind as his mother's. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet to a pre-colonial wreck buried in the floodplain, he has six tides before the monsoon seals it forever. He discovers the vanished team was silenced because they found proof Marisol falsified her life's greatest discovery, and that she is alive, hiding among the salvage crews. In the end Silas chooses truth over legacy: he exposes the forgery and the fleet's corruption together, loses the wreck to the rising water, and gains something rarer — a mother who finally tells him the whole story.
about_author: Paloma Underhill is a former river guide who spent a decade charting seasonal waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels where landscapes remember what people try to forget.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Working a contract survey in the highlands, Silas measures his life in distances covered, avoiding calls from home. A telegram arrives: a government team has vanished in the Verraza valley, and the search coordinator wants him specifically. He burns the telegram but can't sleep. Emotional beat: restlessness curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Gear That Walked Away
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He arrives at the abandoned campsite: tents staked, food cooked, instruments laid out neatly — and no footprints beyond the perimeter, as if eleven people evaporated. Among the equipment he spots a brass caliper with a distinctive repaired handle. His mother's. Emotional beat: recognition as violation; the past reaching out and grabbing him.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Search coordinator Ilsa Reyes's POV. Ilsa briefs Silas: the monsoon arrives in six tides, after which the valley floods and everything below the waterline is unreachable for a year. Worse, the Meridian salvage fleet is already moving upriver, claiming salvage rights over anything the missing team found. Emotional beat: the clock starting, pressure becoming physical.

chapters.title: Reading Water
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas reads the terrain the way others read text — silt lines, broken reeds, a drag mark disguised by rain. The team didn't vanish; they were taken downstream by boat, quietly, at night. Someone wanted them gone without a scene. Emotional beat: competence as identity; for the first time in three years he feels useful.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: New POV: Tomas Beck, Meridian's salvage master. Beck is pragmatic, charming, and utterly corrupt, under orders to reach the wreck first and bury any official report. He learns a government tracker is on the river and smiles — an obstacle is also a resource. Emotional beat: menace wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Downstream of Everything
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Following the river through drowned farmland, Silas finds the first body — or rather, what's left: a surveyor's badge weighted in a fishing net. Not all eleven were taken alive. Grief hardens into anger. Emotional beat: the hunt stops being a job.

chapters.title: What My Mother Taught Me
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Silas's POV. Three years earlier: the fight that ended things — Silas discovered discrepancies in his mother's excavation records and accused her of fraud; she called him ungrateful; he walked out. Now every trail skill he uses is one she taught him. Emotional beat: bitter irony, love tangled with resentment.

chapters.title: The Wreck Beneath the Silt
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Sonar sweeps reveal the target: a pre-colonial trading vessel, intact, buried forty feet down in the floodplain — a discovery worth fortunes and rewriting history books. But the survey data shows anomalies: core samples that don't match the artifacts already catalogued. Emotional beat: wonder undercut by doubt.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Pirates
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Beck intercepts Silas's boat and offers partnership: help me find the site fast, share credit, skip the bureaucracy. Silas refuses and notices, docked behind Beck's flagship, a woman with his mother's posture. He doesn't get a second look. Emotional beat: temptation refused, hope ignited.

chapters.title: Tide Two, Rising
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The river rises faster than forecast; two tides are already gone. Ilsa discovers someone in her own agency leaked the survey route to Meridian — the disappearance wasn't random. She can trust almost no one. Emotional beat: isolation, institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In a flooded-bank village, elders recall another expedition decades ago — Marisol's first — and a local diver who died there. They give Silas a carved token the diver carried, saying the river gives back what is owed. Emotional beat: belonging found among strangers; theme of memory made literal.

chapters.title: Mother, Masked
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, revealed for the first time. Alive and hiding among Meridian's crew under a false name, Marisol has been tracking Beck, knowing he'll lead her to the wreck — and to the evidence that could destroy or redeem her. She sees Silas from a distance and cannot decide whether to run toward him or away. Emotional beat: cowardice and longing in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Forgery
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas recovers the missing team's field notes from a dead drop and finds the truth: Marisol's career-defining artifact was planted, and the vanished team found the proof. Their leader hid it aboard the wreck itself, trusting the river to keep secrets better than governments do. Emotional beat: devastation — his worst accusation was right.

chapters.title: Caught Between Fleets
chapters.summary: Beck's POV. Beck captures Silas, needing his tracking skill for the final approach through the shifting channels. He reveals he knows who Silas is — and that Marisol is aboard, working for him under duress. Leverage complete. Emotional beat: trap closing, power corrupting openly.

chapters.title: Tide Four, Drowning
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa defies orders and takes a small boat upriver, abandoning her career to warn Silas. She finds his abandoned camp and his mother's caliper left deliberately in plain sight — a message. She realizes mother and son are both inside Meridian's net. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over institution.

chapters.title: The Long Dive
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Forced to guide Beck's divers to the wreck, Silas sabotages the descent line subtly, buying hours. Underwater, glimpsing the hull through the murk, he understands why people kill for this: it is beautiful. Emotional beat: awe weaponized against him; resolve forged anyway.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Hold
chapters.summary: Alternating Silas/Marisol POV. Inside the wreck's hold, Marisol breaks cover to stop Beck's men from destroying the evidence samples. Mother and son meet at last, guns and floodwater between them, and she confesses everything in ninety seconds: the forgery, the fear, the years of silence. Emotional beat: catharsis interrupted by crisis.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Comes Early
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The storm hits ahead of schedule; the fifth tide becomes a wall of water. Beck, realizing evidence will exonerate no one including himself, decides to collapse the channel and bury the wreck — and everyone in it. Emotional beat: nature and human greed arriving together.

chapters.title: Six Tides Spent
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Climax: Silas, Marisol, and Ilsa fight through the flooding channels while Beck's crew dynamites the banks. Silas uses every trick his mother ever taught him — and one she never did, reading the flood itself — to get the evidence out and leave Beck's flagship stranded on a sandbar as the river takes its toll. Emotional beat: mastery, fury, forgiveness mid-action.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Aftermath above water: Beck arrested through Ilsa's testimony, the salvage contracts voided, the wreck sealed beneath the new floodline until science, not money, can reach it. The eleven missing: seven accounted for, four lost. Ilsa files the report that ends her career honestly. Emotional beat: grief with integrity.

chapters.title: The Whole Story
chapters.summary: Silas and Marisol's shared POV. On a ridge above the drowned valley, mother and son finally have the conversation three years and one forgery delayed. No absolution offered cheaply; just truth, and the decision to walk the same direction for a while. Emotional beat: reconciliation earned, not given.

chapters.title: A Monsoon for the Trail
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, epilogue. Months later, Silas signs on to the sanctioned recovery effort — not as an escape artist running from miles, but as part of a team measuring time properly. He carries the dead diver's carved token and his mother's caliper. When the next season's rains come, he watches them arrive instead of fleeing them. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, in place and in time.
